title: Machine learning derives an exploratory two-gene signature in gastric cancer
summary: Differential expression and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization on TCGA gastric cancer data prioritized 24 heat-shock-protein-associated genes, consensus clustering defined two molecular clusters, and LASSO-Cox regression derived an exploratory F7-PRNP prognostic signature. siRNA knockdown of F7 or PRNP inhibited proliferation, migration and invasion in HGC27 and AGS cells. The authors state that derivation and evaluation used the same TCGA cohort, so the performance estimates are likely optimistic and independent validation is required; compound prioritization, docking and molecular dynamics are computational only.
ai_technology: LASSO-Cox regression selects the prognostic genes from TCGA transcriptomes; oncoPredict models trained on GDSC2 cell-line data prioritize compounds in silico.
organization: China-Japan Union Hospital of Jilin University, Jilin University

evidence.tested: Signature derived and evaluated within the same TCGA cohort; siRNA knockdown of F7 and PRNP tested in HGC27 and AGS gastric cancer cells.
evidence.unknown: No independent cohort validation; performance estimates likely optimistic; no in vivo or clinical test; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO-Cox regression selected the two genes whose function was then tested by knockdown.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from OpenAlex and Crossref metadata for this DOI; Europe PMC preprint search run. Publisher full text not accessed.
